title: External Web Application Assessment — Northwind Analytics
scope: Public-facing web application and supporting API at https://portal.example.com and https://api.example.com. Social engineering and physical testing explicitly out of scope.
executiveSummary: The assessment identified two high-severity issues in the authentication layer and one medium-severity information disclosure. No evidence of compromise was found in the provided logs. Remediation of the session handling findings should be prioritised before the next release.
methodology: Testing followed the OWASP Testing Guide v4 with manual verification of every automated finding. The engagement combined authenticated and unauthenticated testing across web and API surfaces over five working days.

findings.title: Session cookie missing HttpOnly and SameSite attributes
findings.description: The session cookie is issued without the HttpOnly or SameSite attributes, allowing scripted access to the session token from a cross-site scripting context and lowering the bar for CSRF.
findings.evidence:
Set-Cookie: sid=8f3c2a...; Path=/; Secure

# missing: HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict (or Lax)
findings.remediation: Set HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax (Strict where compatibility allows) on all session cookies, and re-issue active sessions after the change.

findings.title: Broken object level authorisation on export endpoint
findings.description: An authenticated low-privilege user can retrieve report objects belonging to another tenant by incrementing the identifier.
findings.evidence:
GET /v1/reports/1042 HTTP/1.1
Cookie: sid=<low-priv>

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{ "client": "Another Customer Ltd", ... }
findings.remediation: Enforce server-side object ownership checks on every read/write path and add regression tests for cross-tenant identifiers.

findings.title: Verbose error message discloses internal stack trace
findings.description: Unhandled exceptions return a full stack trace including framework versions to unauthenticated callers.
findings.remediation: Return a generic error body with a correlation ID; log full detail server-side only. Confirmed fixed in build 3.4.2.

title: Internal Network Segmentation Review — Harbourline Logistics
scope: Assumed-compromise review of segmentation between the corporate LAN, warehouse floor and OT-adjacent VLANs.
executiveSummary: Initial scoping complete. Two hypotheses are being tested: east-west traffic from the corporate VLAN into warehouse terminals, and flat access from guest Wi-Fi to file services. Fieldwork begins next sprint.
methodology: Document review, firewall rule analysis, controlled reachability testing from four pivot points and validation of alerting coverage for the tested paths.

findings.title: Guest Wi-Fi has unrestricted access to file server SMB
findings.description: The guest wireless network can reach TCP/445 on internal file servers, exposing SMB services to unauthenticated visitors.
findings.evidence:
nmap -Pn -p445,139 --open 10.20.30.10
PORT    STATE SERVICE
445/tcp open  microsoft-ds
findings.remediation: Block guest VLAN to internal RFC1918 ranges at the distribution layer and migrate SMB access behind an authenticated gateway.

findings.title: No east-west flow logging between warehouse VLANs
findings.description: Inter-VLAN traffic is permitted but not logged, leaving lateral movement undetectable after the fact.
findings.evidence: policy: ALLOW any:any vlan41 -> vlan42 (log disabled)
findings.remediation: Enable session logging with 90-day retention for all inter-VLAN rules and stream to the SIEM.
